messages:
samir: Quick RFC follow-up — I prototyped an "attenuation adapter" to sit between the edge proxy and the rate limiter. Goal: smooth short, high-frequency bursts from abusive clients without penalizing normal bursty workloads. Thoughts on interface + tradeoffs?

maria: Nice. Can you sketch the attacker model you optimized for? is this mitigation for low-volume but high-rps clients, or high-volume scraping?

samir: Primary target is low-entropy scraping where a client sends many short requests (small seq_len) to probe endpoints. We want to: 1) avoid immediate hard drops, 2) preserve tail latency for genuine users, 3) degrade gracefully when global capacity is constrained.

aaron: Two obvious design axes: stateful per-client windows vs stateless probabilistic attenuation. Stateful gives better accuracy but harder to scale + more metadata. Probabilistic is cheap but noisy and can hurt legitimate users during correlated spikes.

maria: Agreed. Also need to consider identity surface: user API key vs IP vs signed client-id. Which do we key on for fairness?

jyoti: On infra cost, I'd prefer a hybrid: keep a small LRU per-node sketch (count-min or sliding log) + a short-lived global counter for heavy hitters. That minimizes cross-node sync.

samir: That matches prototype — per-node short windows + a global heavy-hitter bloomfeed. My main open question is the admission interface the rate limiter should expose to the adapter. Two options: (A) opaque score + budget hint, (B) explicit admission decision with suggested fallback.

aaron: If we do (A) the rate limiter remains authoritative; adapter provides hints like "attenuation_score: 0.7" and "suggested_backoff_ms: 200". Rate limiter can ignore or translate. This keeps boundaries clean but requires us to formalize the hint schema.

maria: For (B) adapter would return pre-admit/deny — then the adapter becomes part of the SLO path and we need stricter SLAs on it. I prefer hints (A) unless we can prove low-latency guarantees.

samir: Proposed hint schema (proto-ish):

```yaml
attenuation_hint:
  score: 0.0..1.0   # higher means more likely abusive
  backoff_ms: int   # suggested jitter/backoff per request
  degrade_level: low|medium|high  # how aggressively to escalate
  fingerprint: "sha256:..."  # optional stable client fingerprint
  reason: "replay-detect|pattern-scan|seq-len-anomaly"
```

aaron: LGTM. Add a TTL on fingerprint and make backoff an array for exponential backoff suggestions. Also include a field for whether hint is reversible (so downstream can clear state).

jyoti: Observability: emit attn_score histogram, fingerprint churn, and fraction of requests receiving >0.5 score. Create an alert when attn_score_p95 increases by X% across regions.

ops-bot: dash link -> https://dash.redwood.test/d/abuse/attenuation?refresh=1m  (auto alert: attenuation_p95 > 0.5)

maria: Testing plan: 1) unit tests for hint schema translation, 2) local perf harness to measure added p50/p95 latency (<2ms budget), 3) synthetic attacker replay tests to ensure false-positive rate <0.5% at baseline workloads.

samir: Tradeoffs summary: - Stateful per-node windows: precise, more memory/ops, harder to reason cross-node. - Probabilistic/stateless: cheap, more false positives. - Hint-based interface: clear boundary, rate-limiter decides final action. - Pre-admit interface: simpler for adapter-only enforcement but couples SLAs.

aaron: One more attack vector — multi-client churn trying to poison fingerprints. We should sign/rotate fingerprints per-account and prefer server-derived signals over client-provided.

jyoti: Ops ops: add a kill-switch to disable attenuation adapter per-region; rollback route in console; and a canary rollout with 1% traffic for 24h before 10% -> 50% -> global.

samir: Action items: @maria iterate hint proto + add exponential backoff array (due EOD). @aaron draft perf budget and low-memory sketch proposal (tomorrow). @jyoti wire up dashboards + synthetic tests. I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with the config + sample code.

maria: I'll also add a short section on privacy — fingerprint TTL and KMS notes.

samir: Thanks. If nobody objects I'll start the canary run next Tue. :thumbsup:

aaron: :+1: go for it

jyoti: noted and will prep probe harness

samir: (deleting prototype logs)

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled for 2025-03-04 10:00 UTC (region: us-west-2)
